profile.a: The author summarising his team's solution for the Digital Business 'Green Data' challenge.
Green Data, a hypothetical company running AI for driverless cars, and its partners ARM (low-power chips) and SAC (solar energy).
How to make AI data centres sustainable through AI optimisation, renewable power and new data-centre designs.
Handed in on 18 March 2025; net zero by 2030 and a commercial plan to 2034.
A coastal site in southern England near a solar farm; reference cases in Scotland, Chile, Ireland, the US and Singapore.
Data-centre energy use is expected to double from 2022 to 2026 across about 8,000 data centres, and training one large model emits as much as five cars over their lifetimes.
Weighs AI's carbon cost against its savings, then combines solar sourcing, underwater and natural cooling, reinforcement-learning control and ARM chips, framed as a Massive Transformative Purpose.
